text_blocks.snippet: Effects of COVID-19 on Blood Sugar Levels
COVID-19 infection can affect blood sugar levels, particularly in individuals with pre-existing diabetes or prediabetes.

list.snippet: Studies have shown that COVID-19 infection can lead to increased blood sugar levels, especially in people with diabetes.
This is due to the virus's inflammatory response, which triggers the release of hormones that raise blood sugar.
Additionally, the stress and illness can disrupt insulin production and utilization.
In rare cases, COVID-19 infection can trigger the development of type 2 diabetes in individuals who previously did not have it.
This is thought to be related to the virus's damage to the pancreas, which produces insulin.
Even in people without diabetes, COVID-19 can cause elevated blood sugar levels.
This is more common in individuals with severe infections or obesity.
If you have diabetes and test positive for COVID-19, it's important to monitor your blood sugar levels closely and follow your doctor's instructions.
You may need to adjust your insulin dosage or medication.
Non-diabetic individuals with elevated blood sugar levels should also consult their healthcare provider for evaluation and management.
The effects of COVID-19 on blood sugar levels can vary depending on the severity of the infection, the individual's health status, and any pre-existing conditions.
It's important to stay informed about the latest research and guidance from healthcare professionals.
